summary: Isaline Blew Horner was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She studied at Newnham College, the University of Cambridge, and under Caroline Rhys Davids. She held positions at Newnham College, Cambridge, and served as Honorary Secretary of the Pali Text Society.
Iselin Frydenlund is a religious and Buddhist studies scholar. In 2016, she was attested as a senior researcher at the Peace Research Institute Oslo and a Research Fellow at the University of Oslo.

Ishtiaq Hussain Qureshi was a history, archaeology, and Indology scholar. He studied at St. Stephen's College and the University of Cambridge, holding posts at St. Stephen's, University of the Punjab, Columbia University, University of Karachi, and the National Language Promotion Department.

Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Educated at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Benares Sanskrit College, and Sanskrit College and University, he served at Fort William College, Sanskrit College and University, and became Direktor at Benares Sanskrit College.

Iso Kern is a philosopher, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Louvain, Freiburg, Heidelberg, National Taiwan University, and Columbia. His posts include KU Leuven, University of Heidelberg, University of Bern, and teaching appointments at Zurich and Fribourg.
Issaen Ikeyama is a Buddhist studies scholar who was attested in 1976 as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji Junior College.
Issei Suzuki was a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University, where he also held a position as a professor.
Issei Yamakawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed his studies at Sophia University and earned a master's degree at Aichi Gakuin University.
Itsuko Nishikawa is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at Teachers College, Columbia University, taught Qian Lin, and held a post at the University of Washington.

Ivan Minayev was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg from circa 1858 to 1862 and held a post on its Faculty of Oriental Studies from circa 1871 to 1890.

Ivan Pavlovich Minaev was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at the University of Saint Petersburg and under Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev and Albrecht Weber, later serving as a professor at the University of Saint Petersburg.

Ives Goddard is a linguist who studied at Harvard College and Harvard University. He held academic posts at Harvard University (circa 1966–1970) and worked at the Smithsonian Institution and National Museum of Natural History from circa 1970 to 2025.
Ives Waldo is a scholar of philosophy, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Oxford and studied under traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa.

Ivette Vargas-O'Bryan specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, Charles Hallisey, Kurtis R. Schaeffer, and Theodore Riccardi, and held a fellowship post at Grinnell College.

Ivo Fišer was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer at the University of Prague (attested 1960) and held a post at the University of Copenhagen's Institute for Indian Philology (attested 1970).

Iwao Nakajima is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nikki Kimura and earned a master's at Hitotsubashi University. He held posts at the NHK Broadcasting Culture Research Institute until 1975 and at Sandhaan (attested 1999).

Iwao Shima was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Nagoya University from circa 1969 to 1978 and held academic posts at Kanazawa University from circa 1989, becoming a professor in circa 1996.

Izumi Hoshi is a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who completed undergraduate and graduate studies at the University of Tokyo. Since 1997, she has held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, including assistant professor and director.
Izumi Matsuda-Kiami is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, held a post at the University of Washington, and taught Qian Lin.

J. A. B. van Buitenen was an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He held positions at Deccan College, Utrecht University, and the University of Chicago.
